Hi Marissa —

Thanks for taking a look. Quick summary of what we plan to run in the POC / pilot:
- Model family: open-llama-70b variant (we expect to use the 70B architecture with a KV cache tweak to support extended context).
- Typical context: up to 70k tokens for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + user prompt; average length per request ~ 15k tokens, 95th percentile ~ 52k tokens.
- QPS target: 8 steady qps during business hours; occasional spikes to 18 qps for short bursts.
- Quality requirement: can't quantize below 8-bit for our highest-sensitivity calls; we are OK with int8-ish on lower-fidelity routes.
- Expected concurrency: planning for 2 logical routes — "high-fidelity" (30% of traffic) and "economy" (70%).

Could you provide a dedicated capacity recommendation (pods / GPU count), plus how that changes if we: 1) enable 4-bit quant on economy traffic, 2) use a KV offload to host-side for tail contexts, or 3) cap per-request context at 40k tokens?

Attached the workload summary and an example prompt profile. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Sofia

Folks —

I ran a quick projection based on our OL-70B profile and the token distributions in Sofia's CSV. High-level numbers, per-request peak GPU RAM (working set including KV + activations + model params):
- 70k context, FP16: ~95 GB working set -> requires a 96GB A100-class partition (effectively 1 full GPU for capacity but no headroom) ; KV + activation growth during bursts pushes effective need toward 1.6 GPUs to meet latency.
- 70k context, int8 (symmetric quant): ~64 GB working set -> fits in 80GB-class GPUs with ~1.2 GPU effective need under steady qps; spikes need additional headroom.
- 70k context, 4-bit (aggressive): ~46 GB working set -> fits comfortably in 48GB GPUs but expect quality loss for high-fidelity route (Sofia already noted sensitivity).

Edge cases / offload impact:
- KV offload to host (pinned NVMe + page cache) reduces GPU resident KV by ~30-40% in our microbenchmarks, saving ~15-25 GB on the 70k case but adds ~12-18ms tail latency on cold prefixes. Good compromise for economy route.
- Capping effective per-request context at 40k tokens drops working set roughly proportional to KV reduction; FP16 case falls to ~60 GB working set, making 80GB GPUs sensible for high-fidelity with ~1.3x headroom.

Recommendations for sizing math inputs:
- Use candid conservative headroom factor of 1.6x for guaranteed latency SLOs, and 1.25x for cost-optimized commitments.
- For reserved capacity proposals, present both FP16-reserved baseline and int8-reserved baseline so procurement can see delta.

I'll hand off the detailed spreadsheet numbers to Priyom — includes per-GPU QPS for our typical batching curve.

-Rishi

Marissa / team / Sofia —

Attached is the short plan (summary below). I focused on three offerable SKUs we can present in the SOW: FP16-conservative, int8-balanced, and mixed-route-optimized. Numbers assume US region, reserved monthly commit with 24/7 baseline.

Summary (rounded / per node math):
- Workload assumptions: 8 steady qps, 18 spike qps; 30% high-fidelity traffic with 70k median KV, 70% economy traffic with 15k median KV.

SKU A — FP16 conservative (SLA-backed):
- GPU class: 96GB A100 equivalent
- Reserved: 6 GPUs (handles 8 qps steady with 1.6x headroom for latency SLO at 70k contexts)
- Burst headroom: +3 GPUs shared across pool
- Notes: highest quality, no aggressive quantization; KV-in-GPU for high-fid route.

SKU B — int8 balanced (cost-savings):
- GPU class: 80GB / 80GB-equivalent
- Reserved: 4 GPUs (handles steady workload using int8 on economy route, high-fid still FP16 on dedicated partition)
- Burst headroom: +2 GPUs
- Notes: ~30% cost reduction vs FP16 baseline on unit economics; requires validation on fidelity-sensitive prompts but should pass most evals.

SKU C — mixed-route optimized (recommended for POC):
- GPU mix: 2 x 96GB reserved for high-fid + 3 x 48-80GB for economy (with int8 / 4-bit experiments)
- Burst headroom: +3 GPUs (elastic policy)
- KV strategy: keep full KV in-GPU for high-fid; offload economy KV to host-NVMe with async warm caching; cap economy context at 40k for heavy tails.
- Operational: route by intent classifier, canary for quantized variants, auto-fallback to FP16 high-fid if regression detected.

Engineering / rollout notes:
- Canary plan: route 5% traffic to int8 variant for 48 hours, compare quality metrics vs baseline. If regression < 1.5% top-level metric delta, expand to 25% then 60%.
- Cost delta: SKU B saves ~28% on GPU-hours vs SKU A; SKU C splits savings and risk.

Next steps: Marissa — if Sofia signs off, I'll prepare an SOW with per-month committed GPU counts and a 30-day SLA addendum. Sofia — confirm whether procurement needs an explicit on-prem KV-offload security assessment (host NVMe encryption) and if your team prefers 40k hard cap or dynamic policy.

Thanks —
